evidence_candidates.text:
ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOLOK CITY
NUMBER 2 OF 2020
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improvement of Services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in their region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the Right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the Right to survival, growth and development as well as the Right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, particularly against Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the Solok City region. Solok City is one of the parties most authorized in carrying out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations in order to provide guarantees for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of Solok City. The regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women and Children victims of Violence.

Article 9
The community in the context of preventing the occurrence of violence against women is responsible for:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to the occurrence of violence against women;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing the occurrence of unregistered marriages.

CHAPTER VI
HANDLING OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE First Part General

Article 26
Children in conflict with the law, children who experience pregnancy outside of marriage, children who are victims of human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome transmission, and children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances abuse are protected in their rights to obtain education.

Article 13
Regional Governments in their efforts to guarantee, protect and fulfill children's rights are responsible for establishing and implementing policies for the protection and fulfillment of children's rights which include the areas of birth registration, health, education, employment and social affairs.

Article 57
(1) The Regional Government conducts supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children.
(2) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year by the Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are in the field of supervision.
(3) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy on protection of women and children in the Region.

1.6.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 9 huruf c says the community should "mencegah terjadinya pernikahan di bawah tangan" (prevent unregistered/under-the-table marriages). This is not a policy provision that recognizes/permits a harmful practice; it is a prevention measure. The judge treated the mere mention of unregistered marriage as evidence that the policy covers “harmful practices” (as if endorsing or addressing them as a form of violence), but the passage is about preventing it. With the retrieved passage, a careful reading should not automatically flip the indicator to Yes unless the indicator is defined as ‘mentions harmful practices to prevent them’—but given the golden label is No, the judge’s interpretation was too broad.

2.1.evaluator_rationale: The provided passages describe roles and responsibilities of the City of Solok Regional Government and cooperation with community/private/NGOs, but do not mention coordination or cooperation with other governments across jurisdictions.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Solok.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Solok.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination whether in the form of preventive, repressive, or postremedial protection.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
7. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and the state.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
10. Street Child is a child whose life is irregular by spending most of their time outside the home to seek livelihood on the streets or in public places.
11. Regional Child Forum hereinafter referred to as Forda is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems
13. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Assistance is all actions taken in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social rehabilitation for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence;
16. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women, physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and the community.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
21. Social Rehabilitation is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
22. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.

Article 29
(1) Every person or entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.
(2) The worst forms of work as referred to in paragraph (1) are: a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices; b. all work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances or gambling;
c. all work that exploits, provides, or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of children.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 56
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance on the implementation of protection of women and children.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. conducting socialization of programs and activities for the protection of women and children; and
b. providing training for government officials, law enforcers, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers regarding prevention and handling of violence against women and children.

2.1.rationale: The Indonesian regulation does not set out an inter-institutional coordination mechanism across jurisdictions (e.g., coordination with provincial/national governments or other districts) nor a formal network/coordination body. It does mention cooperation with private sector/LSM (Pasal 12 ayat (1) huruf e; ayat (2)) and cooperation with masyarakat/ormas (e.g., Pasal 38 ayat (1) huruf d), and it lists multiple service providers for complaint handling (Pasal 43), but these are not clearly framed as a coordination mechanism/network across institutions/governments. The judge’s No is consistent with both the retrieved English and the Indonesian source; thus the golden label ‘Yes’ appears incorrect for this document.

4.4.rationale: The retrieved evidence (Pasal 24) is about non-discriminatory access to education and provision of educators for children with disabilities/special talents. In the Indonesian source, Pasal 24 indeed concerns education access/equality, not education-based violence-prevention programming (e.g., curriculum on GBV prevention, consent, gender equality, anti-violence education). There are prevention/socialization provisions elsewhere (e.g., Pasal 7 huruf a about sosialisasi pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan; Pasal 14 huruf c about sosialisasi/edukasi hak anak), but the judge specifically relied on Pasal 24, which does not establish prevention-through-education against violence. So the judge overgeneralized ‘education policy’ as ‘violence prevention through education,’ producing a false positive.

5.1.rationale: The Indonesian regulation does explicitly mention collaboration with NGOs/LSM: Pasal 12 ayat (1) huruf e states the Regional Government shall "melakukan kerjasama dengan pihak swasta dan/atau lembaga swadaya masyarakat" (cooperate with the private sector and/or NGOs) for fulfilling children’s rights. This exact content was present in the retrieved English passage [2.1-27] (though shown under a different discrepancy, it is the same document text). For this indicator’s retrieval set, however, the candidates shown to the judge for 5.1 did not include Pasal 12; they focused on community participation and other provisions. Given the judge said “none explicitly mention NGOs,” the immediate cause is that the judge missed that “organisasi kemasyarakatan” can include NGOs, but more importantly the clearest NGO term “lembaga swadaya masyarakat” was not surfaced in the candidates for 5.1. Still, because the judge had passages about cooperation with community organizations and could have been more flexible, this is best characterized as evaluation failure (overly strict reading of what counts as NGO collaboration) rather than translation error.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOLOK CITY
NUMBER 2 OF 2020
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improvement of Services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in their region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the Right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the Right to survival, growth and development as well as the Right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, particularly against Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the Solok City region. Solok City is one of the parties most authorized in carrying out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations in order to provide guarantees for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of Solok City. The regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women and Children victims of Violence.

The judge’s Yes is supported by the source, so the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.
